objects.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
objects.why: The nearest big galaxy, a naked-eye cloud from the southern hemisphere, and the reason the ladder has a local-group rung at all.

objects.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
objects.why: The Large Cloud's smaller companion, a naked-eye smudge from the south, and the pair that gave the Magellanic Stream its name.

objects.name: Fornax Dwarf
objects.why: A faint satellite of the Milky Way with six globular clusters of its own -- a small galaxy that kept its jewellery.

objects.name: Sculptor Dwarf
objects.why: The first dwarf spheroidal galaxy ever found (1937): so sparse that Shapley took it for a smudge on the plate.

objects.name: Carina Dwarf
objects.why: A faint Milky Way satellite whose stars formed in several distinct bursts -- a small galaxy with a stop-start history.

objects.name: Draco Dwarf
objects.why: One of the most dark-matter-dominated galaxies known: its stars move far too fast for the light we see.

objects.name: Ursa Minor Dwarf
objects.why: A near neighbour of the Milky Way whose stars are almost all ancient -- it stopped forming them early.

objects.name: Sextans Dwarf
objects.why: So diffuse it was only found in 1990, on photographic plates scanned by machine.

objects.name: Leo I
objects.why: Sits in the glare of Regulus, one of the brightest stars in the sky, which hid it for decades.

objects.name: Leo II
objects.why: Leo I's fainter neighbour on the sky, a dwarf spheroidal found on the same 1950 survey plates.

objects.name: Barnard's Galaxy
objects.why: The first galaxy beyond the Milky Way whose distance was measured -- Hubble's 1925 proof that other galaxies exist.

objects.name: IC 10
objects.why: The Local Group's only starburst galaxy, seen dimly through the dust of the Milky Way's own disc.

objects.name: IC 1613
objects.why: A quiet irregular dwarf so free of dust that it anchors the Cepheid distance scale.

objects.name: Wolf-Lundmark-Melotte
objects.why: An isolated dwarf at the edge of the Local Group that has lived its whole life alone.
